note: Uh-Oh Courtyard: What Would You Do? Choices are shuffled at render; every choice gets warm spoken feedback; the best choice gets confetti. No negative sounds.

scenarios.text: Your friend has a toy you want. They are still playing with it.

choices.text: Ask: "Can I have a turn when you're done?"
choices.feedback: Asking nicely shows respect. Great choice!
Grabbing hurts feelings. Asking works better.
That is okay too. You could also ask for a turn.

scenarios.text: Someone cuts in front of you in line.

choices.text: Say: "I was here. Please go behind me."
choices.feedback: Calm words and honest. Well done.
Pushing can hurt. Words work better.
Telling a grown-up is fine. Try your words first.

scenarios.text: You broke your sister's favorite toy by accident.

choices.text: Say sorry and offer to help fix it
choices.feedback: Sorry and helping. So kind.
Hiding makes it worse. Honest is braver.
Good. And say sorry to your sister too.

scenarios.text: Your friend falls and scrapes a knee.

choices.text: Ask if they are okay and get help
choices.feedback: Caring and helpful. Perfect.
Laughing hurts more. Kindness helps.
Checking on a friend is the kind thing to do.

scenarios.text: Someone says your drawing is silly.

choices.feedback: You know your own heart. Strong!
Your art is worth keeping.
Walking away is okay. Standing up for your drawing is even better.

scenarios.text: Your brother knocks down your blocks. You feel very mad.

choices.text: Take space and breathe, then use words
choices.feedback: Cool down first. Then words. Wonderful.
Hitting hurts. Breathing helps.
A grown-up can help. Try a breath first.

scenarios.text: The work is hard and you want to quit.

choices.text: Say: "This is hard. Can you help me?"
choices.feedback: Asking for help keeps you going.
Hard is okay. Help is near.

choices.text: Take a break and come back
choices.feedback: Breaks help. Then ask for help.

scenarios.text: A new kid sits alone at lunch.

choices.text: Say hi and ask them to sit with you
choices.feedback: You made a new friend feel welcome.
Everyone likes to be included.
A smile is nice. An invitation is even nicer.

scenarios.text: You lose a game and feel upset.

choices.feedback: That is a good sport. Luna loves it.
Losing is part of playing. Try again.
Breathing helps. Then say good game.

scenarios.text: You spill your milk at the table.

choices.feedback: Accidents happen. Helping is great.
Honesty feels better.
It is okay to be upset. Then help clean up.

scenarios.text: Someone wants a turn on the swing you are using.

choices.text: Say: "Five more swings, then it's your turn."
choices.feedback: Fair and kind. Sharing turns.
Turns make playgrounds happy.
Kind! You can also finish a few swings first.

scenarios.text: It is dark and you feel scared.

choices.text: Tell a grown-up and ask for a night light
choices.feedback: Asking for what you need is brave.
It is okay to feel scared. A grown-up can help.
Breathing helps a lot. Then ask for help.

choices.text: Ask: "Are you okay? Want to play with me?"
choices.feedback: A caring friend. That is you.
Sad friends need company.
Hugs are nice. Ask first.

scenarios.text: You get an answer wrong in front of the class.

choices.feedback: Mistakes help us learn. Brave!

choices.text: Say you never want to answer again
choices.feedback: Everyone makes mistakes. Keep trying.
That is okay. Trying again is even better.

scenarios.text: You cannot find your shoes and it is time to go.

choices.feedback: Asking for help solves it fast.
Screaming makes it harder to find them.
Good idea. Then ask for help.

scenarios.text: The room is too loud and your ears hurt.

choices.text: Say: "It is too loud for me. Can I take a break?"
choices.feedback: You know what your body needs.
More noise makes it worse.
That helps. Asking for a break helps more.
